title: A mark in the margin
hints: Look at the dots, not the gaps in the circle.
There are nine dots. The envelope uses Roman numerals.
Nine is written IX.
revelation: IX is a catalogue identifier. It is not a security clearance or a military code.

title: The word that survived
hints: The missing word is also something left behind.
It starts with T and ends in E.
The word is TRACE.
revelation: TRACE is a public catalogue tag. It leads to a foundation page, not a secret computer system.

title: The shelf index
hints: Start with rows or boxes that have two empty cells. Pencil marks can help.
The first row is 1, 2, 3, 4.
The full grid is 1234 / 3412 / 2143 / 4321. The marked diagonal reads 1441.
revelation: The completed diagonal reads 1441. Shelf 1441 opens three independent research threads.

title: Four letters on the receiver
hints: Each wide pause separates a letter. There are four letters.
The groups are . / -.-. / .... / ---.
The decoded marker is ECHO.
revelation: The receiver carried ECHO. That is an observed marker, not proof of a prediction.

title: Three places to the left
hints: This is a Caesar shift, not an unfamiliar military cipher.
Shift D back three letters to A. Do the same for the other letters.
The message reads DO NOT TRUST THE DATE.
revelation: Voss warned that the date labels themselves needed verification.

title: Two dates, two meanings
hints: Find the words “opened for signature” and “entered into force”. They refer to different events.
1972 is the signature year. The later date is the one the question asks for.
The convention entered into force in 1975.
revelation: The Aster label conflated signature in 1972 with entry into force in 1975.

title: The institution and the speech
hints: The speech and the agency’s establishment are separate milestones.
1953 belongs to Atoms for Peace. Follow the timeline to the agency.
The IAEA was established in 1957.
revelation: Aster’s chart used the speech’s year as the institution’s founding year.

title: The two halves of an order
hints: The cross marks, not the paper edges, are the alignment references.
The correct position is 62% across and 38% down on the inspection mat.
Align at 62 / 38. The signature is ROOK.
revelation: Elias Rook requested retrospective date labels. This establishes editorial intent, not responsibility for historical events.

title: Which record is primary?
hints: The press summary and typed copy were created after the editorial memorandum.
The IX receipt matches the original receiver-log digest. A matching digest establishes the file’s identity, not that every interpretation is true.
Select the original receipt labelled IX.
revelation: IX preserves the original log and the editorial history. It separates a manufactured prediction claim from the unexplained ECHO marker.

title: The ninth record
hints: Your board has three conclusions: an editorial method, an original record, and an unresolved observation.
Rook requested retrospective dates; Voss retained IX; Hale recorded ECHO.
The answers are BACKDATING, IX, and ECHO.
revelation: You have documented the retrospective date changes, preserved the original IX log, and left ECHO as an open research question.

title: A note behind the page
hints: On most desktop browsers, use View Page Source from the browser menu. This is optional.
Search the source text for “conservator”.
The comment’s reference word is LANTERN.
revelation: The source comment is Voss’s mundane breadcrumb: a reference to the desk lamp, not an intrusion into a real system.

title: A different alphabet each time
hints: Repeat ECHO beneath the ciphertext. Convert A–Z to 0–25.
Subtract each key value from the matching ciphertext value, wrapping around the alphabet.
The plaintext is REMEMBER.
revelation: REMEMBER is Hale’s instruction to preserve the original observations, including the ones that do not fit a theory.
